qt: to the Commission Elena Kountoura (The Left), Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) Subject:

Following a previous question1 on the need to support Greek and European beekeeping, the situation facing the sector remains critical and European support remains inadequate. In its reply2, the Commission referred to the existing support tools that are available through the 2023-2027 CAP and stated that it would continue to work with Member States and industry representatives to consider further support measures. However, the new funding structure for the 2028-2034 CAP, which will be delivered through the National and Regional Partnership Plans, raises legitimate concerns among industry representatives3 about maintaining the current distinct European financial framework for beekeeping4. It seems that, from now on, the support offered will be at the discretion of each Member State, with no European guarantees and guaranteed minimum allocations. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it intend to support the preservation of the special funding envelope for beekeeping with sufficient and guaranteed financial support within the new 2028-2034 CAP funding structure?

What measures does it intend to take under the new CAP to support the granting of annual subsidies for individual beehives for pollination services and to ensure both that they are adequately funded and that beekeepers from all Member States have equal access?
What initiatives will it take to support the beekeeping sector in Greece, where the effects of climate change are particularly acute?

at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.10.2026) The Commission’s proposal for the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP)1 under the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) (2028-2034) does not propose specific Union-level financial allocations for individual agricultural sectors. This is in part to support the intentions of increased flexibility and simplification under the next MFF, allowing Member States to determine allocations, depending on their specific needs and challenges. However, apiculture is recognised as important in contributing to achieving the CAP objectives, and therefore support for the sector s remains mandatory2. Thus, all Member States must reserve a specific Union budget for apiculture interventions in their National and Regional Partnership (NRP) plans3. This amount will be doubled through national funds, since the minimum national contribution should at least equal the Union financial assistance4. Although the proposal does not introduce an annual subsidy for pollination, Member States could also support the sector through other CAP interventions. These can include annual payments for agri-environment and climate actions for beekeepers who voluntarily undertake commitments benefiting the environment and/or biodiversity. In addition, coupled income support for farmers could in future be extended to apiculture products in case the sector is identified by the Member States as facing difficulties5. The proposals are currently being negotiated by the European Parliament and the Council under the ordinary legislative procedure and are subject to the outcomes of the negotiations. Greece would also be required to implement apiculture interventions, which can include support for actions aimed at mitigating and/or adapting to climate change6.
